ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r3.claim: Tadhkira means reminder: the Qur'an recalls truths already present in human nature rather than imposing an alien teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r3.anchor: its purpose too is precisely the same.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r4.claim: Qur'anic reminders draw arguments from the inner and outer worlds, reason, familiar history, and teachings to which the audience claims descent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r4.anchor: which these addressees claimed to be a progeny and followers of.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r5.claim: The object of 'fear' is omitted; parallel Qur'anic wording supplies 'their Lord unseen,' as in al-Baqarah 2:2.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r5.anchor: The grammatical object of the verb

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r6.claim: Piety is natural where human nature remains sound; Qur'anic reminders awaken such people, while those who have corrupted their nature remain unmoved.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r6.anchor: As for those who pervert their natures

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r1.claim: People who demand sensory proof understand only force, but God values belief acknowledged through intellect rather than observation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r1.anchor: before God, only that belief has weight

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r2.claim: Since the Qur'an is a reminder, the Prophet's task is to remind rather than coerce; whether people benefit is their responsibility, so their failure should not distress him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p8/r2.anchor: the responsibility of the people and not his.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says tadhkiratan can substitute for li-tashqā or follow an omitted “but We sent it as a reminder.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r3.anchor: إلا تذكرة يصح أن ينصب على البدل من موضع لتشقى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects substitution because the accusatives differ in kind, treating illā as a disconnected exception meaning “but.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r4.anchor: لا لاختلاف الجنسين ولكنها نصب على الاستثناء المنقطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says li-tashqā has no syntactic case position for tadhkiratan to replace; he rejects strained alternative parses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r5.anchor: والذي نقول إنه ليس له محل ألبتة فيتوهم البدل منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also says the Quran brings burdens of delivery, argument, conflict, and prophetic duties so it may serve as reminder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r6.anchor: أنزلنا إليك القرآن لتحمل متاعب التبليغ ومقاولة العتاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r7.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r7.claim: They allow tadhkiratan as apposition to al-Qurʾān or as a verbal noun; Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects a purpose-object analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r7.anchor: وأجاز هو وأبو البقاء أن يكون مصدرا أي لكن ذكرنا به تذكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r8.claim: Fear of God motivates faith and righteous action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r8.anchor: والخشية باعثة على الإيمان والعمل الصالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers parses for tanzīlan as apposition, an omitted verb, a complement of anzalnā, emphasis, or an object of yakhs͑ā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r2.anchor: في نصب تنزيلا وجوه أن يكون بدلا من تذكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds the alternatives strained: the verbal nouns do not naturally form this apposition, one reading loses restriction, and others are distant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r3.anchor: والأحسن ما قدمناه أولا من أنه منصوب بنزل مضمرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r4.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r4.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads tanzīlun in the nominative with implicit huwa, detaching it from yakhs͑ā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p311/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة تنزيل رفعا على إضمار هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p312/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p312/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p312/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests anzalnā might quote Gabriel and the descending angels; Abū Ḥayyān says God is the apparent speaker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p312/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ويجوز أن يكون أنزلنا حكاية لكلام جبريل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r1.claim: The clause means the Quran was sent down as an admonition for whoever fears God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r1.anchor: أي لكن أنزلناه عظة لمن يخشى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r2.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r2.claim: An alternate parsing says the Quran was not sent to make Muhammad suffer; it was sent only as a reminder for the Godfearing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p263/r2.anchor: وقيل: تقديره ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r2.claim: The reminder points to people promised glad tidings at the preceding surah's close: the community will include enough pious believers to match the Qur'an's miraculous stature and endurance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r2.anchor: ممن أشرنا في آخر التي قبلها إلى بشارته إيماء إلى أنه سيكون فيهم من المتقين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an gathers laws, counsel, spiritual insights, knowledge, manners, histories, and interests of both worlds from earlier scriptures, and exceeds them; the community's size reflects its book's greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r3.anchor: أي أعظم الكتب , الجامع لكل خير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r4.claim: Illā here means but; a poetic line illustrates an exception that functions as a qualification of praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r4.anchor: غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r5.claim: Illā tadhkiratan may be an accusative substitute for the position of la-tashqā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r5.anchor: أن ينصب على البدل من موضع لتشقى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r6.claim: Alternatively, it may depend on an implicit verb meaning rather, We sent it down as a reminder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r6.anchor: ويصح أن ينصب بفعل مضمر تقديره لكن أنزلناه تذكرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r7.claim: The word khashyā includes faith and righteous action because fear motivates them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r7.anchor: ويخشى يتضمن الإيمان والعمل الصالح إذ الخشية باعثة على ذلك

MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.claim: Ṭā Hā functions like the disconnected letters opening other sūrahs, with the same introductory function.
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.anchor: ساكن لأنه جرى مجرى فواتح سائر السور اللواتى مجازهن مجاز حروف التهجي ومجاز موضعه فى المعنى كمجاز ابتداء فواتح سائر السور

MAJAZ:v2p15/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p15/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p15/r4.claim: The verse uses fronting and postponement with an understood pronoun; it can mean the Qur'an was sent down as a reminder for the God-fearing, not to cause hardship, or that a reminder was sent down separately from the hardship clause.
MAJAZ:v2p15/r4.anchor: مجازُه مجاز المقدم والمؤخر وفيه ضمير، وله موضع آخر من المختصر الذي فيه ضمير

JISHUMI:v6p4628/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r9.claim: Tadhkira is exposing someone to a reminder or explanation.
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r9.anchor: والتذكرة: التعريض لذكر البيان، ذكره تذكيرا وتذكرة.

JISHUMI:v6p4628/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r15.claim: Tadhkiratan is accusative as the object of anzalnā; alternatively, an omitted verb is understood: “We sent it down as a reminder.”
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r15.anchor: (تذكرة) نصب ب (أنزلنا)، وقيل: لمحذوف تقديره: أنزلناه تذكرة.

JISHUMI:v6p4636/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r6.claim: The word tadhkira requires reflection; those who fear are singled out as beneficiaries, though the Quran reminds everyone.
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r6.anchor: ويدل قوله: تذكرة على وجوب التفكر فيه، وإنما خص من خشي لأنهم المنتفعون وإلا فهو تذكرة للجميع.

NAHHAS:v3p31/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p31/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p31/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq treats tadhkiratan as an apposition to yashqā, meaning the Qur’an was sent only as a reminder.
NAHHAS:v3p31/r11.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هو بدل من يشقى أي ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة

NAHHAS:v3p31/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p31/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p31/r12.claim: The author calls that analysis remote and prefers an accusative verbal noun or an accusative of purpose.
NAHHAS:v3p31/r12.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا وجه بعيد والقريب أنه منصوب على المصدر أو مفعول من أجله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r1.speaker: بعض النحويين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r1.claim: Some grammarians call the lām in li-tashqā a negative lām, while others call it lām al-juhūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r1.anchor: قال النحاس: بعض النحويين يقول هذه لام النفي، وبعضهم يقول لام الجحود.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن بن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysan calls it a genitive lām, yielding the meaning that the Qur'an was not revealed to make the Prophet suffer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r2.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر: وسمعت أبا الحسن بن كيسان يقول: إنها لام الخفض، والمعنى ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن للشقاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r3.claim: Shaqāʾ may be pronounced long or short, comes from a wāw-root, and means hardship and toil.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r3.anchor: والشقاء يمد ويقصر. وهو من ذوات الواو. وأصل الشقاء في اللغة العناء والتعب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r4.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r4.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates that even the intelligent may suffer in ease while the ignorant enjoy happiness.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ذو العقل يشقى في النعيم بعقله
وأخو الجهالة في الشقاوة ينعم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r5.claim: Here li-tashqā means the Prophet should not exhaust himself grieving and regretting the disbelievers' rejection; his duty is to convey and exhort, not guarantee their belief.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r5.anchor:
فمعنى لتشقى «لتتعب» بفرط تأسفك عليهم وعلى كفرهم، وتحسرك على أن يؤمنوا كقوله تعالى:
فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم
[الكهف: 6] أي ما عليك إلا أن تبلغ وتذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r6.speaker: أبو جهل والنضر بن الحارث
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r6.claim: Abu Jahl and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith called the Prophet wretched for abandoning his fathers' religion; the verse answers that Islam and Qur'an lead to success and happiness, while unbelief is true misery.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r6.anchor: وروي أن أبا جهل بن هشام لعنه الله تعالى والنضر بن الحارث قالا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنك شقي لأنك تركت دين آبائك فأريد رد ذلك بأن دين الإسلام وهذا القرآن هو السلم إلى نيل كل فوز

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r7.speaker: جبريل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r7.claim: An alternative occasion says the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled, and Gabriel told him to spare himself because his body had rights; the verse means the Qur'an did not come to exhaust him in worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r7.anchor: وعلى الأقوال المتقدمة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام صلى بالليل حتى اسمغدت قدماه فقال له جبريل: أبق على نفسك فإن لها عليك حقا أي ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتنهك نفسك في العبادة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r8.claim: This alternative frames the mission as the easy, upright religion rather than a demand for punishing exertion.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats tadhkiratan as an exception replacing tashqā, meaning that the Qur'an was revealed only as a reminder.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r9.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الزجاج: هو بدل من «تشقى» أي ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r10.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas calls that grammatical analysis remote, and Abu Ali rejects it because a reminder is not a form of suffering.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r10.anchor: النحاس: وهذا وجه بعيد وأنكره أبو علي من أجل أن التذكرة ليست بشقاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r11.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas instead analyzes tadhkiratan as a cognate accusative or purpose object: the Qur'an was sent to remind, not to cause hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r11.anchor: وإنما هو منصوب على المصدر، أي أنزلناه لتذكر به تذكرة، أو على المفعول من أجله، أي ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى به، ما أنزلناه إلا للتذكرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r12.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r12.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl proposes reordered syntax: the Qur'an was revealed as a reminder to the God-fearing and not to make the Prophet suffer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:3-6/r12.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: فيه تقديم وتأخير، مجازه: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى، ولئلا تشقى.

TABATABAI:20:8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8/r6.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:20:8/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes afterlife and worldly misery, with worldly misery divided into psychological, bodily, and external forms; he relays the view that misery can mean toil, though all misery is toil but not all toil is misery.
TABATABAI:20:8/r6.anchor: والشقاوة كالسعادة من حيث الإضافة فكما أن السعادة في الأصل ضربان سعادة أخروية وسعادة دنيوية

TABATABAI:20:8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8/r7.claim: In this context, the verse means that the Quran was not sent down to make the Prophet toil by straining himself to compel people to accept it.
TABATABAI:20:8/r7.anchor: فالمعنى ما أنزلنا القرآن لتتعب نفسك في سبيل تبليغه بالتكلف في حمل الناس عليه

TABATABAI:20:8#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r1.claim: Turning away from a truth is called forgetting by a deliberate extension because both have the same effect: failing to attend to it.
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r1.anchor: وإنما سمي نسيانا بنوع من العناية وهو اشتراكهما في الأثر وهو عدم الاعتناء بشأنه

TABATABAI:20:8#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r2.claim: Fear of the consequences of heedlessness and indulging worldly desire is needed to jolt the soul toward truth, allowing the reminder to benefit its hearer.
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r2.anchor: فلا بد في دفع هذا النسيان الذي أوجبه اتباع الهوى والانكباب على الدنيا من أمر ينتزع النفس انتزاعا

TABATABAI:20:8#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r3.claim: Those who fear are people disposed to respond: when they hear truth, latent fear appears, so they believe and become mindful.
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r3.anchor: وأن المراد بمن يخشى من كان في طبعه ذلك، بأن كان مستعدا لظهور الخشية في قلبه

TABATABAI:20:8#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r4.claim: The exception is disconnected: the Quran was not sent to burden the Prophet but to serve as a reminder that leads those inclined to fear toward belief and piety.
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتتعب به نفسك ولكن ليكون مذكرا يتذكر به من شأنه أن يخشى

TABATABAI:20:8#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r5.claim: Grammatically, tadhkira is an active verbal noun and the purpose of the sending; tanzīlan is a passive verbal noun used circumstantially for the pronoun referring to the Quran, meaning a divine revelation that reminds the fearful.
TABATABAI:20:8#2/r5.anchor: مصدرا بمعنى الفاعل ومفعولا له لقوله

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.claim: The narrative's fit with the surrounding verses, taken in their context, is unclear.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.anchor: أن في انطباق الآيات بما لها من السياق على القصة خفاء

TABRISI:20:2-8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:2-8/r4.claim: The Qurʾān was not sent to make the Prophet toil so intensely; it is a reminder for whoever fears God.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r4.anchor: وذكر أنه ما أنزل عليه الوحي ليتعب كل هذا التعب

TABRISI:20:2-8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r5.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:20:2-8/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad takes the phrase to mean, rather, that God sent the Qurʾān as a reminder; tadhkirah is a verbal noun like tadhkīr.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r5.anchor: قال المبرد: معناه لكن أنزلناه تذكرة

THALABI:v6p237/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p237/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet and companions tied ropes across their chests for night prayer, thinking it obligatory, and the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p237/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه يربطون الحبال في صدورهم في الصلاة بالليل ذلك بالفرض، وأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.

THALABI:v6p237/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r10.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v6p237/r10.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl proposes fronting and postponement: the meaning is that the Qur'an was sent as a reminder to the fearful so the Prophet would not suffer; tanẓīlan is apposition to tadhkira.
THALABI:v6p237/r10.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: فيه تقديم وتأخير مجازه: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى ولئلا تشقى، تنزيلا بدل من قوله تذكرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r3.claim: The Quran is a reminder and admonition for whoever fears God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r3.anchor: أي: ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة، موعظة { لمن يخشى } يخاف الله عز وجل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p252/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p252/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p252/r1.claim: The revelation is a reminder for those who fear God, while the disbeliever does not accept the reminder.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p252/r1.anchor: قوله: {إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى} [طه: 3] يقول: وإنما أنزله الله تبارك وتعالى تذكرة لمن يخشى الله، وأما الكافر فلم يقبل التذكرة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses تذكرة as a purpose object of revelation, alongside لتشقى; the first requires lām because it lacks the conditions for a bare object, while the second may omit it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r1.anchor: والثاني جاز قطع اللام عنه ونصبه لاستجماعه الشرائط. هذا كلام الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa objects that revelation already has the purpose-object لتشقى and therefore cannot take تذكرة as another purpose-object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r3.anchor: قد منع أبو البقاء أن تكون " تذكرة " مفعولا له لأنزلنا المذكورة، لأنها قد تعدت إلى مفعول له

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r4.claim: The author rejects Abu al-Baqa's restriction: an action may have two or more purposes; the restriction assumes only one such adjunct is allowed.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r4.anchor: وهذا المنع ليس بشيء؛ لأنه يجوز أن يعلل الفعل بعلتين فأكثر

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj, followed by Ibn Atiyya, treats تذكرة as a substitute for the case position of لتشقى; Abu Jaʿfar regards this as unlikely and al-Farisi rejects it because reminder is not misery.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r5.anchor: أن تكون " تذكرة " بدلا من محل " لتشقى " وهو رأي الزجاج، وتبعه ابن عطية، واستبعده أبو جعفر، ورده الفارسي

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects substitution because reminder and misery differ in kind, and instead reads إلا as a disconnected exception meaning لكن.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r6.anchor: وقد أوضح الزمخشري هذا فقال: " فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن تكون

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r7.claim: The Shaykh says the different kinds are the basic accusative of تذكرة versus the apparent accusative of لتشقى after dropping a preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r7.anchor: قال الشيخ: " يعني باختلاف الجنسين أن نصبة " تذكرة " نصبة صحيحة ليست بعارضة

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r8.claim: The author says al-Zamakhshari means al-Farisi's semantic point, that reminder is not misery, and asks how different accusatives affect substitution.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r8.anchor: ليس مراد الزمخشري باختلاف الجنسين إلا ما ذكرته عن الفارسي ردا على الزجاج، وأي أثر لاختلاف النصبين في ذلك؟

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r9.claim: Another parse makes تذكرة a disconnected exception: revelation was sent down, but as a reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r9.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا على الاستثناء المنقطع أي: لكن أنزلناه تذكرة

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r10.claim: It may instead be a verbal noun emphasizing an omitted verb, estimated as لكن ذكرنا or تذكر به أنت.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r10.anchor: أنه مصدر مؤكد لفعل مقدر، أي: لكن ذكرنا، أو تذكر به أنت تذكرة

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r11.claim: Another analysis treats تذكرة as a verbal noun used circumstantially, meaning except as one reminding.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r11.anchor: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال أي: إلا مذكرا

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r12.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r12.claim: Al-Hawfi makes تذكرة an apposition to القرآن, since the Qur'an itself is a reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r12.anchor: أنه بدل من " القرآن " ، ويكون القرآن هو التذكرة، قاله الحوفي

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also lets لتشقى govern تذكرة: the Qur'an makes the Prophet bear the toil of preaching and confronting opponents so that it may be a reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r13.anchor: السابع: أنه مفعول له أيضا، ولكن العامل فيه " لتشقى " ويكون المعنى كما قال الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r1.claim: لمن يخشى attaches to تذكرة; the lām reinforces the verbal noun's government, or the phrase may modify an omitted adjective of تذكرة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r1.anchor: و { لمن يخشى } متصل ب " تذكرة ". وزيدت اللام في المفعول تقوية للعامل لكونه فرعا

SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r2.claim: On the previously described analysis, تذكرة may be circumstantial as well as a purpose object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه يجوز أن يكون " تذكرة " حالا ومفعولا له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r1.claim: Alusi parses tadhkiratan as an accusative of discontinuous exception: the Quran was sent not to make the Prophet suffer, but as a reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r1.anchor: نصب على الأستثناء المنقطع أي ما انزلناه لشقائك لكن تذكيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r2.claim: Those who fear are people disposed to fear God and respond to warning because of tender hearts and gentle temperaments.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r2.anchor: أي لمن شأنه أن يخشى الله تعالى ويتاثر بالانذار لرقة قليه ولين عريكته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means those whom God knows will fear when warned.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r3.anchor: أو لمن علم الله تعالى أنه يخشى بالتخويف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r4.claim: The prepositional phrase attaches either to tadhkirah or to an omitted adjective describing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r4.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بتذكرة أو بمحذوف صفة لها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r5.claim: The fearful are singled out although the Quran reminds everyone because those who do not benefit are treated as nonexistent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r5.anchor: وخص الخاشبى بالذكر مع أن القإن تذكرة للناس كلهم لتنزيل غيره منزلة العدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows tadhkiratan as a purpose object of anzalna, accusative because its governing conditions are met; the first purpose phrase lacks a shared agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r6.anchor: وجوز الزمخشرى كون تذكرة مفعولا له لانزلنا وانتصب لاستجماع الشرائط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r7.claim: Multiple purpose clauses may occur without coordination or substitution when their grammatical relations differ, as here; Alusi gives further examples of such causes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز تعدد العلة بدون عطف وابدال إذا اختلفت جهة العمل كما هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r8.claim: On the purpose-object reading, revelation's hardships serve as a reminder; the Prophet has borne enough strain in conveying it and should not exhaust himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r8.anchor: وفي الكشف أن المعنى على هذا الوجه ما انزلناه عليك لتحتمل مشاقه ومتاعبه إلا ليكون تذكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r9.claim: An objection says the analogy with striking for discipline except compassion requires a causal relation between the two purposes, absent between hardship and reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r9.anchor: واعترض القول بجعله نظير ما ضربتك للتاديب إلا اشفاقا بأنه يجب في ذلك أن يكون بين العلتين ملابسة بالسببية والمسببية حتما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r10.claim: The objection says this reading would fit if the exception meant increasing the Prophet's reward, since reward is proportional to effort, as a hadith states.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150#2/r10.anchor: إلا تكثيرا لثوابك فان الاجر بقدر التعب كما في الحديث انتهى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r1.claim: Alusi answers that a causal link between the purposes need not be required, or that reminder itself entails toil, as the exposition's summary suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r1.anchor: ولعل قائل ذلك يمنع وجوب أن يكون بين العلتين الملابسة المذكورة أو يدعى تحققها بينهما في الآية بناء على أن التذكرة أي التذكير سبب للتعب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r2.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r2.claim: Ibn al-Munir finds the reading remote: it makes hardship the cause of revelation, and says a noncausal or consequential lam misses God's usual consoling the Prophet, against the cited consolation passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r2.anchor: على ابن المنير فقال : أن فيه بعدا لأنه حينئذ يكون الشقاء سبب النزول وان لم تكن اللام سببية وكانت للصيرورة مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r3.claim: Alusi says that once the intended meaning is understood, the alleged contradiction with the Prophet's other consolation passages disappears.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r3.anchor: وانت تعلم بعد الوقوف على المراد أن لا منافاة نعم بعد هذا الوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r4.claim: Tadhkirah may be a circumstantial accusative of the addressee or Quran, with a free exception and the verbal noun understood adjectivally or intensively.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون حالا من الكاف أو القرآن والاستئناء مفرغ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r5.claim: Al-Hufi treats tadhkirah as a substitute for al-Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r5.anchor: وجوز الحوفى كونها بدلا من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats tadhkirah as a substitute for the syntactic position of litashqa.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r6.anchor: والزجاج كونها بدلا من محل ( لتشقى ) لأن الاستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r7.claim: Alusi rejects substitution: a substitute after exception requires a connected exception, but reminder and hardship are not of one kind; Abu Ali also rejected al-Zajjaj's analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r7.anchor: وبالجمله هذا الوجه ليس بالوجية وقد انكره أبو على على الزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r8.claim: Another analysis makes tadhkirah a purpose object of revelation and litashqa an adjective of Quran, but requires an omitted relative construction and an unusual definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يكون مفعولا له لانزلنا و ( لتشقى ) ظرف مستقر في موضع الصفة للقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r9.claim: A further proposal takes tadhkirah as the source of an omitted verb, meaning, rather, We reminded you with a reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p151/r9.anchor: وقيل : هي نصب على المصدرية لمحذوف أي لاكن ذكرناه به تذكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.claim: One esoteric reading says the reminder recalls the days of union before souls entered bodies and promises their return; alternatively, it reminds them of those days to stir longing, tears, and effort toward regaining them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.anchor: أي إلا لتذكر من يخشى ايام الوصال التى كانت قبل تعلق الأرواح بالابدان وتخبرهم بانها يحصل نحوها لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.claim: Some identify those who fear as scholars, citing 35:28; since knowledge can invite vanity and pride, the reminder of God’s greatness protects scholars from these faults.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r7.anchor: من يخشى هم العلماء لقوله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r1.claim: The phrase means rather a reminder, as a disconnected exception; it cannot be an appositive to li-tashqā because the categories differ, nor a second direct purpose of one verb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r1.anchor: { إلا تذكرة } لكن تذكيرا، وانتصابها على الاستثناء المنقطع، ولا يجوز أن يكون بدلا من محل { لتشقى } لاختلاف الجنسين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is a verbal noun used circumstantially, or a purpose attached to Qur’an through an understood adjective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r2.anchor: وقيل هو مصدر في موقع الحال من الكاف أو القرآن، أو مفعول له على أن { لتشقى } متعلق بمحذوف هو صفة القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r3.claim: A single verb cannot directly take two purpose clauses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r3.anchor: فإن الفعل الواحد لا يتعدى إلى علتين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r4.claim: The reminder benefits a tender-hearted person affected by warning, or one God knows will fear when warned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:3/r4.anchor: { لمن يخشى } لمن في قلبه خشية ورقة تتأثر بالإنذار، أو لمن علم الله منه أنه يخشى بالتخويف منه

DURR-FULL:v5p551/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r3.claim: Qatada says God sent the Book and messengers as mercy, so a listener may remember and benefit; the Qur’an is a reminder containing lawful and forbidden matters.
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى}

BURSEVI:v5p279/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p279/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p279/r1.claim: Tadhkiratan is accusative as the purpose of revelation, coordinated in meaning with the negated tashaqqā through a disconnected exception; one verb has two purposes only by substitution or coordination.
BURSEVI:v5p279/r1.anchor: نصب على أنه مفعول له لأنزلنا معطوف على تشقى بحسب المعنى بعد نفيه بطريق الاستدراك

BURSEVI:v5p279/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p279/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p279/r2.claim: The Qur’an was sent as reminder and admonition for those God knows will fear when reminded and warned, rather than to burden the Prophet in its delivery.
BURSEVI:v5p279/r2.anchor: ولكن تذكيرا وموعظة لمن يعلم الله منه أن يخشى بالتذكرة والتخويف

BURSEVI:v5p279/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p279/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p279/r3.claim: Although reminder and proclamation are universal, the verse singles out those who benefit from them, consistent with the Qur’an being a warning to all worlds.
BURSEVI:v5p279/r3.anchor: وتخصيصها بهم مع عموم التذكرة والتبليغ لقوله تعالى : {ليكون للعالمين نذيرا}

BURSEVI:v5p279/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p279/r4.speaker: الكبير
BURSEVI:v5p279/r4.claim: Al-Kabīr says the Messenger is included among those who fear, indeed foremost in fear and in receiving the reminder.
BURSEVI:v5p279/r4.anchor: قال في "الكبير" ويدخل تحت قوله : {لمن يخشى} الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.claim: The ending closes the debate and echoes the opening: the Prophet has delivered guidance, so he may take comfort in completing his mission while the heedless remain astray until truth becomes clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.anchor: وهي قوله { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى } ( طه : 2 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#3/r1.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#3/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash parses ‘as a reminder’ as an apposition to ‘toil’: the Quran was not sent down except as admonition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إلا تذكرة قال الأخفش هو بدل من قوله لتشقى ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة أي عظة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272#2/r1.claim: God sent the Book and messengers as mercy, so those who remember may benefit from hearing His reminder, which sets out what is lawful and forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272#2/r1.anchor: رحمة، رحم بها العباد، ليتذكر ذاكر، وينتفع رجل بما سمع من كتاب الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r13.claim: The Quran is a warning for whoever fears God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, it is a rebuke that restrains the God-fearing from sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r15.claim: Fear concerns causes that are apparent, whereas reverent fear concerns causes that are not apparent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r15.anchor: والفرق بين الخشية والخوف : أن الخوف فيما ظهرت أسبابه والخشية فيما لم تظهر أسبابه

MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.claim: The Quran was sent as a reminder for whoever fears God, from the Creator of the earth and seven high heavens, not to make Muhammad suffer.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r1.claim: The exception is disconnected, meaning rather it was sent as a reminder; alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r1.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن انزلناه تذكرة أو حال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r2.claim: The reminder is for one who fears God, or whose eventual outcome is fear.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#3/r2.anchor: لمن يخاف الله أو لمن يؤل أمره إلى الخشية

QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.claim: Spiritual discipline has already produced in the Prophet the two qualities signified by those names, making him perfected and perfecting; hard hearts explain why his guidance has no effect.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.anchor: ما المقصود بالرياضة إلا هذان الأمران اللذان ظهرا فيك تجلينا عليك بالاسمين المذكورين

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.claim: Another reading of the address is: do not distress yourself grieving over their disbelief; the Qur'an was sent as a reminder, and each person's belief or unbelief concerns that person, while Muhammad must only deliver.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد لا تشق على نفسك ولا تعذبها بالأسف على كفر هؤلاء فإنا إنما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتذكر به

QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r12.claim: The Quran gives insight to people of understanding and reminder to people of spiritual arrival: the former gain future relief, the latter immediate intimacy.
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r12.anchor: فالقرآن تبصرة لذوي العقول ، تذكرة لذوي الوصول

STUDYQURAN:20:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r1.claim: “But” may mean “however,” making verse 3 a turn rather than a direct continuation of verse 2.
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r1.anchor: But in v. 3 can mean “however,” which would indicate that v. 3 does not directly follow upon v. 2

STUDYQURAN:20:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r2.claim: If read continuously with verse 2, the Quran was sent not to cause hardship but as a reminder to one who fears God.
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r2.anchor: the Quran was not revealed to the Prophet in order to cause him hardship, but rather was sent down only as a reminder

STUDYQURAN:20:3/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r3.claim: Those who fear are the God-revering muttaqīn; Reminder is also a name for the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:20:3/r3.anchor: one who fears refers to those who reverence God

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r1.claim: The Quran is a reminder for those who fear God; they benefit from the revelation that sets out what is lawful and forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r1.anchor: ليتذكر ذاكر، وينتفع رجل بما سمع من كتاب الله، وهو ذكر له أنزل الله فيه حلاله وحرامه

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r2.claim: Qatadah says the revealed books and sent messengers are God's mercy to people, so they remember and benefit from scripture, which sets out the lawful and forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى} [طه: 3] وإن الله أنزل كتبه، وبعث رسله

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the revelation is a reminder for whoever fears.
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى} [طه: 3] قال: الذي أنزلناه عليك تذكرة لمن يخشى

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r4.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r4.claim: Some Basran grammarians parse “reminder” as an appositive to “to make you suffer,” yielding “We sent it down only as a reminder.”
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r4.anchor: بعض نحويي البصرة يقول: قال: إلا تذكرة

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r5.claim: Some Kufan grammarians parse the accusative as governed by an understood “We sent it down.”
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r5.anchor: بعض نحويي الكوفة يقول: نصبت على قوله: ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r6.claim: Some reject apposition to the negated “to make you suffer” because the exception is affirmative, describing the wording instead as repetition.
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r6.anchor: وكان بعضهم ينكر قول القائل: نصبت بدلا من قوله {لتشقى} [طه: 2] ويقول: ذلك غير جائز، لأن {لتشقى} [طه: 2] في الجحد، و {إلا تذكرة} [طه: 3] في التحقيق، ولكنه تكرير

TAB-FULL:v16p10/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r7.claim: Others construe the sense as “We sent down the Quran only as a reminder for one who fears, not to make you suffer.”
TAB-FULL:v16p10/r7.anchor: وكان بعضهم يقول: معنى الكلام: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى، لا لتشقى

SULAMI:v1p434#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r1.claim: Ibn Ata addresses Muhammad as the leader of the fearful: the Quran was sent as a reminder for him to find repose and relief from fear, since a lover finds intimacy in the beloved's book and words.
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : قيل له : يا محمد أنت إمام

SULAMI:v1p434#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r2.claim: Ja'far says the Quran is admonition for the fearful, mercy for sinners, and intimacy for lovers.
SULAMI:v1p434#3/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : أنزل الله القرآن موعظة للخائفين ورحمة

TABRISI:20:1-2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:1-2/r15.claim: Tadhkiratan is a purpose object, and liman yakhshā is a prepositional phrase functioning as an adjective for reminder.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r15.anchor: تذكرة مفعول له. لمن يخشى الجار والمجرور في موضع الصفة لتذكرة

TABRISI:20:1-2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:1-2/r16.claim: The better analysis makes tadhkiratan a verbal noun from an omitted verb and treats the exception as disconnected: “but as a reminder.”
TABRISI:20:1-2/r16.anchor: والأولى أن يكون مصدر فعل محذوف ويكون الاستثناء منقطعا والتقدير لكن تذكرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r1.claim: Al-Farra reads the accusative as if the phrase said, “We sent it down only as a reminder,” supplying an omitted verb from the context.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: (نصبها على قوله: ما أنزلناه إلا تذكرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad takes the phrase as “but a reminder,” supplying “We sent it down”; he compares the ellipsis in 92:19–20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p352/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: (لكن تذكرة أي: لكن أنزلناه تذكرة، كقوله تعالى:

ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.claim: These reports clarify that reading Qur’an and tafsir aims at reminding those who fear God: the Qur’an was not sent to impose hardship, but as a reminder for the God-fearing.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.anchor: Bununla Kur’an ve tefsir okumaktan maksad ne olduğunu da anlamış oluyoruz.

ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.claim: Elmalılı prays that God illuminate their hearts with the light of the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.anchor: Heman Cenâb-ı Allah kalblerimizi nûr-i Kur’an ile tenvîr buyursun.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s message is not meant to extinguish the joy of life; it guides, reminds, and warns those who accept their human responsibility and fear failing it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.anchor: yaratılış amacına uygun bir sorumluluk bilinci taşıyanlara yol göstermek, hatırlatma ve uyarılarda bulunmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.claim: In context, the passage consoles a demoralized Prophet and implies he should not ruin himself over people who resist truth and worship handmade idols; the reminder benefits those conscious of responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.anchor: mâneviyat kırıklığına uğrayan Hz. Peygamber’e teselli verildiği, Kur’an’ın, ancak insan olmanın sorumluluğunu taşıyanlar

BURHAN:v4p235/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p235/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p235/r9.claim: تذكرة may be parsed as an accusative substitute for لتشقى, yielding the sense that the Quran was sent down only as a reminder.
BURHAN:v4p235/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ﴿ تذكرة ﴾ بدلا من ﴿ لتشقى ﴾

RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.claim: He exemplifies identical ending letters with the linked endings in the opening of Ṭā Hā and the opening of al-Ṭūr.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.anchor: فالحروف المتجانسة كقوله تعالى: {طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى}. الآيات. وكقوله: {والطور وكتاب مسطور}
